obligation: FSIS notification of adulterated or misbranded product in commerce
trigger: A plant learns or determines that adulterated or misbranded meat product it produced has entered commerce (for example, product shipped from Plants 2 or 5 after CCP monitoring stopped or after an unexplained formulation change, and evaluation finds it adulterated)
deadline: Within 24 hours of learning or determining; include type, amount, origin, and destination of the product
notify: FSIS District Office for each affected plant
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all six plants are official establishments
notifying_entity: Each affected plant (plant FSQA manager with the Division VP FSQA)
clock_starts: Learning or determining that product in commerce is adulterated or misbranded

obligation: HACCP corrective action for an unforeseen deviation (product decision, not a notice)
trigger: Loss of CCP monitoring or suspected tampering with cook, chill, cold storage, or formulation controls
deadline: Segregate and hold affected product; review its acceptability; prevent adulterated product from entering commerce; reassess the HACCP plan. Records available to FSIS (417.5(f))
notify: Internal; FSIS inspection program personnel on site review records
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all six plants
clock_starts: Start of the deviation (last trusted CCP record)

obligation: Reportable Food Registry
trigger: A responsible party (the registrant of a registered facility where the food is manufactured, processed, packed, or held) determines an article of food is a reportable food: reasonable probability of serious adverse health consequences or death
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 24 hours after the determination. No report if the adulteration originated with the responsible party, was detected before any transfer, and was corrected or the food destroyed (350f(d)(2))
notify: FDA through the Reportable Food Registry portal; investigate the cause
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Plant 6 and the five DCs (registered facilities); not Plants 1 to 5 or the stores
notifying_entity: Plant 6 FSQA manager; Division food safety manager (Distribution)
clock_starts: Determination that the food is a reportable food

obligation: Corrective action on loss of temperature control at a DC (product decision, not a notice)
trigger: Loss of temperature control that may affect the safety of refrigerated packaged food (including loss of monitoring that hides an excursion)
deadline: Correct the problem; evaluate all affected food; prevent food from entering commerce unless it is shown not adulterated; keep records (117.206(a)(5))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - five DCs
clock_starts: Indication of loss of temperature control

obligation: Possible material failure of temperature control during transport
trigger: Shipper, loader, receiver, or carrier becomes aware of an indication of a possible material failure of temperature control (for example, loads whose telematics alerts were lost)
deadline: Food must not be sold or distributed unless a qualified individual determines it was not rendered unsafe; communicate with other parties as necessary
notify: Receivers of the affected loads (group stores, independent grocers, food service customers, 3PL customers)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Food Distribution as shipper, carrier, and receiver; stores as receivers
notifying_entity: Fleet director with the Division food safety manager (Distribution)

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example, employee names with Social Security numbers). The current definition in 501.171(1)(g)1. also covers biometric data and geolocation, which matters for driver telematics data; a name with email, phone, and address only is not personal information
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 additional days for good cause if the Department is told in writing within 30 days (applies only to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - employee data of each employing division; worked example for every state
notifying_entity: Each employing entity (division or corporate) with the Group General Counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination (no good-cause extension for this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 26,000 Florida employees in the exercise scenario

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if more than 1,000 Floridians are notified
clock_starts: Decision to notify more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (inbound)
trigger: A vendor maintaining personal information for the group (payroll vendor, loyalty platform vendor, telematics vendor) has a breach
deadline: The third-party agent must notify the covered entity within 10 days following determination of the breach
notify: The affected division and the Group General Counsel
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts

obligation: Breach notice in each other state where affected individuals reside
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information as each state defines it (current and former employees live in many states; loyalty members mainly in the five operating states)
deadline: Varies by state (for example, "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days); some states also require attorney general or regulator notice
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state; counsel checks whether loyalty contact data is personal information in any state
notifying_entity: Group General Counsel with each employing entity

obligation: Disclosure committee escalation (internal)
trigger: Severity 1 incident declared
deadline: Within 24 hours of declaration
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - group policy

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: The disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination; delay only if the U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure update
trigger: Annual report after a significant incident
deadline: In the next Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: Card brand compromise reporting: Visa worked example (contractual)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.1-A.3 and A.5; Visa Core Rules 10.3.1.2. Card brand rules applied through the acquirer, not law. Other brands' rules not verified
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that stores, processes or transmits it
deadline: Tell the acquirer immediately (A.3.1). Make sure the event is reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation (A.1.1), then send the incident report within 3 calendar days of that notice (A.2.1). If Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator, retain one within 5 business days (A.5.1.1)
notify: Acquirer; Visa Global Risk Investigations, through the acquirer. Other brands as the acquirer directs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Grocery Retail is a merchant
clock_starts: Suspicion or confirmation of the compromise

obligation: Forensic investigation for a suspected card compromise: Visa worked example (contractual)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.5 and A.6. Card brand rules applied through the acquirer, not law. Other brands' rules not verified
trigger: Formal notice from Visa that a PCI Forensic Investigator (PFI) or an Independent Investigation is required
deadline: Within 5 business days of Visa's notice, retain the PFI (or, for an Independent Investigation, a qualified investigator) and tell Visa the firm and lead investigator; tell the acquirer too when a PFI is retained (A.5.1.1, A.6.1.1). An event not contained within 60 business days may lead Visa to require a PFI (A.6.1.3)
notify: Visa (firm and lead investigator); the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Conditional - only if card compromise is suspected

obligation: 3PL customer incident notice
trigger: Incident affecting a customer's data, inventory records, or temperature history, or product held for that customer
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery under the standard 3PL agreement (company contract term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 60 external brands at DC-1 and DC-3
notifying_entity: 3PL services director with the Group General Counsel

obligation: Customer notice under supply agreements
citation: Supply and quality agreements with independent grocers, food service customers, and private-label retailers (contract)
trigger: Incident affecting deliveries, product safety, or any recall
deadline: Per each agreement (commonly prompt notice of any recall or food safety event)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; Meat Processing and Food Distribution keep the lists

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties
notifying_entity: Group General Counsel with the board risk committee

obligation: Voluntary report to FBI and CISA
trigger: Ransomware or another significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as practicable (Day 0 to Day 1 in the runbook)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; supports OFAC mitigation and may bring OT response help

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment is disbursed (proposed)
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. As proposed, the group would be covered (it exceeds the SBA size standard for its NAICS codes). Recheck when final

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers by a financial institution under FTC jurisdiction
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - no division is a financial institution under the rule (the co-branded card is issued by a partner bank)

obligation: Reporting of cyber incidents at MTSA facilities
trigger: Cyber incident at an MTSA-regulated facility
deadline: Immediately (6.16-1); without delay to the National Response Center for entities not reporting under 6.16-1
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or the National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group has no MTSA-regulated facility

obligation: Covered telecommunications / Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) and FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day for covered telecommunications (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: DFARS cyber incident report
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - no defense contracts

obligation: Ammonia release reporting (only if the incident causes a release)
citation: Not verified in this sample (federal and state release-reporting rules for anhydrous ammonia)
trigger: Loss of refrigeration control leads to an ammonia release at a plant or DC
deadline: Not stated here; follow the site PSM and RMP emergency response plan
notify: Per the site emergency response plan
applies_at_this_tier: Conditional - refrigeration controls are in scope of the incident

obligation: Brief FSIS inspection program personnel on site (practice, not a stated rule)
citation: Plant practice under the HACCP and recall procedures
trigger: Electronic CCP monitoring is down and manual monitoring and holds are in place
deadline: At once, before the next scheduled task
notify: FSIS inspection program personnel at the affected plants
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - practice at all six plants

obligation: FDA food facility registration update
trigger: Not triggered by an incident; listed so the team does not confuse registration duties with incident notices
deadline: Renewal between October 1 and December 31 of each even-numbered year
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Plant 6 and five DCs; no incident clock
notifying_entity: Plant 6 plant manager; Division food safety manager (Distribution)
